chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevaktil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri quoted Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Maymun, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them) who said:

Jesus the son of Mary (peace be upon him) said: 'Blessed is he whose silence is contemplation, whose gaze is a lesson, whose spaciousness is his home, and who weeps over his sin. And from whom people are safe from his hand and his tongue.'

key_terms.وَسْعُهُ بَيْتَهُ: Contentment with one's home/spaciousness of home

ai.seo_question: What are the five characteristics of the blessed according to Jesus ibn Maryam in this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq attributes this profound ethical maxim to Jesus (Isa) via the Prophet Muhammad and the Imams, highlighting the continuity of prophetic wisdom in Shia tradition. The narration emphasizes inner contemplation and social harmony, linking personal piety (silence, reflection) with communal peace (safety from hand and tongue), a key theme in al-Khisal's discussion of blessed conduct.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-63 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Maymun , on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (MGB) that

Jesus the son of Mary (MGB) said, “Blessed be those who have five characteristics. Blessed be those who think when they are silent; who get advice by looking; who sit at home and cry over their sins; and do not bother the people with their hands or tongues.”
